name: Ansible SSH host-key verification disabled
attack_scenario: an attacker who can redirect the target hostname/IP (DNS poisoning, BGP hijack, malicious jump host) transparently MITMs the SSH session, capturing sudo passwords and injecting commands, and the play never notices the changed host key
negative_test_hint: present a swapped host key "AAAAForgedAttackerHostKey" from a MITM endpoint and assert the play fails host-key verification instead of connecting and sending credentials

exemplar.explanation: StrictHostKeyChecking=no (or host_key_checking: false, or git accept_hostkey: yes) makes Ansible connect to any host without verifying its SSH key, defeating the protection known_hosts provides. accept-new pins the key on first use instead of blindly trusting every future key, and the value 'accept-new' does not match the =no pattern so the safe form is clean.
